めし屋ひろし.name: Meshiya Hiroshi
めし屋ひろし.desc: A "meshiya" (eatery) boasting an overwhelming variety across 14 pages of menus. Everything from set meals with free rice refills to all-you-can-drink at night. The jiggly, melt-in-your-mouth pig's feet (tebichi) soba pairs well with a generous helping of green onions.
t: I ate here in January 2024. This shop was a participant in the "13th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally (2023.10.1–2024.2.29)", and I went as my 32nd of 34 shops 😊
Meshiya Hiroshi
Once again I came here before my hobby of surfing (Itoman City: Suicide Cliff point). To match the 11:30 opening time, I waited in the parking lot in front of the shop from about 11:15 😄
Then a staff member noticed me and called out to me around 11:20, about 10 minutes before opening, and I went inside as the first customer of the day 😆
I had decided to order whatever was featured in the stamp rally booklet, so I ordered the "tebichi soba" without even looking at the menu in the shop.
While I was ordering I checked the menu, and it's quite extensive 😄
Menu (it opens straight with set meals. It was also written on the sign outside, but it seems rice refills are free. A recommended shop for people who want to eat heartily lol)
Menu (lots of rice bowls too lol)
Menu (the Okinawa soba menu comes on the 3rd page)
Menu (the 4th page is set meals. Looks delicious 😋)
Menu (the 5th page is also set meals 😆)
Menu (the 6th page is soups and rice bowls)
Menu (the 7th page is billed as curry and light meals, but they just look like hearty rice dishes to me (^0^;) Okinawa champon is the best 😄)
Menu (the 8th page is the takeout menu (bento). What a rich menu 😆)
Menu (the 9th page is also the takeout menu (à la carte). What a rich menu 😆)
Menu (the 10th page is the all-you-can-drink menu. Nights are well covered too 😆)
Menu (the 11th page is also the all-you-can-drink menu. Nights are well covered 😆)
Menu (the 12th page is the night drinks menu 😆)
Menu (the 13th page is the night snacks-with-drinks menu 😆)
Menu (the 14th page is the night à la carte dishes menu 😆)
Inside Meshiya Hiroshi

Wow, just as I finished photographing the menus, the "tebichi soba" I ordered arrived right away 😆 At "Warai Soba", where I ate yesterday, I was also the first customer, but the waiting time was completely different. You want to eat Okinawa soba quickly and casually, and here they were fully prepared and it came right away lol. Impressive.
Tebichi soba (medium) ¥880
First I taste the soup 😆 It's a relatively light pork bone broth with a slight pork bone kick. Simply tasty.
Tebichi soba (medium) ¥880
Next I try the noodles. The medium-thick wavy noodles have a soft texture, and since there's plenty of green onion, eating the crunchy onions together with the noodles works nicely 😆
The pig's feet (tebichi) topping is really jiggly and melt-in-your-mouth, and simply delicious. It melts in your mouth almost like a drink 😋
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. True to the shop name "meshiya" (eatery), it's not just Okinawa soba — the other menu items are quite extensive too.

やかそば.name: Yaka Soba
やかそば.desc: A shop along Route 329 in Matsuda, Ginoza Village. You can choose thin or flat noodles, and bonito powder is sprinkled over the bonito broth to bring out the bonito flavor. Chewy noodles and three tender soft-bone pork ribs make for a hearty bowl. A good stop on an east-coast drive.
t: I went to eat here in June 2022 😄
Yaka Soba (along Route 329)
Yaka soba ¥830

I ordered the "Yaka soba", which shares the shop's name. You can choose between thin and flat noodles, and I went with the recommended flat noodles. On top of the bonito broth, bonito powder is sprinkled over it, which really brings out the bonito flavor. The noodles had good chewiness, the soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were tender, and there were three of them, so it was hearty too 😊
Rating (9/15): Hearty and delicious. How about it when you're driving the east coast of the northern region 😁

やまや.name: Yamaya
やまや.desc: A shop in Kumoji marked by its red awning. The signature Yamaya soba has a blended broth with a hint of pork bone and medium-thin, gently wavy flat noodles. Pairing it with the handmade mozuku kimchi, which was featured on Matsuko's TV show, is fun too.
t: *This article was partly made by AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), and I added and updated some parts myself lol
Hello! I'd like to introduce the Okinawa soba at "Yamaya" in Kumoji, Naha City 😊 I ate here in October 2024 😄

On this Okinawa soba tour, I visited "Yamaya" in Kumoji, Naha City. Actually, today I had planned to eat at "Kiseki no Tebasaki", a stamp rally participant, but unexpectedly it was closed 😅 So I hurriedly decided to go to "Yamaya" nearby instead.
Yamaya
Menu
Menu
Menu
Menu (this mozuku kimchi was apparently featured on Matsuko's TV show)

When you step inside, in contrast to the exterior with its striking red awning, the atmosphere is calm. Looking at the menu, the "Yamaya soba", which shares the shop's name, catches the eye as the signature item. I had no choice but to order it 😄
Yamaya soba (large) ¥870
The "Yamaya soba" was brought out promptly. First, the homemade soup. It's a blended broth with a faint pork bone flavor, gentle in taste. Simply tasty.
Yamaya soba (large) ¥870

Next I try the noodles. Medium-thin flat noodles with a gentle wave and a softish texture. They cling well to the soup and are easy to eat. The braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) is also tender, with just the right amount of chew 😋

This shop is actually famous for its handmade kimchi, and the mozuku kimchi in particular has apparently been featured on national TV, including Matsuko's show. The kimchi that came as a side dish this time was less spicy than I expected, with a gentle seasoning. I think it's a flavor even tourists will find easy to eat.
Rating (9/15): Overall, simply tasty Okinawa soba. The new style of enjoying it together with kimchi is interesting too. If you come to Kumoji in Naha City, why not drop by? 😊

ゆうなみ坂下店.name: Yunami Sakashita Branch
ゆうなみ坂下店.desc: Its selling point is homemade fresh noodles, with a choice of flat, thin, or yomogi (mugwort) noodles. The bonito broth and firm yomogi noodles are top-tier delicious. The complimentary fuchiba (mugwort) on the table is a nice touch.
t: I ate here in December 2022 ☺ I was drawn in by the "homemade fresh noodles" on the sign 😁
Yunami Sakashita Branch
I ordered the soki soba.
Soki soba
There's fuchiba (mugwort) for topping placed on the table, which is nice ☺

The soup with a strong bonito broth is delicious 😋 You can choose flat, thin, or yomogi noodles, and this time I chose the yomogi noodles. Homemade fresh noodles with strong chewiness and a mugwort aroma — the noodles are delicious too. Unfortunately, though, the pork spare ribs (soki) were dry and bland, so tasteless that I wondered, "Were they not seasoned yet?"

Rating (9.5/15): Wow, the noodles and soup were really delicious, and I thought they were top tier compared to other shops, but unexpectedly the topping (soki) had no flavor and felt dry, which is such a shame. If the soki were delicious too, I think it would be at the level of a "shop that holds its own against the recommended ones".

ゆたかやそば.name: Yutakaya Soba
ゆたかやそば.desc: A popular shop in a picturesque red-tiled old house (originally in Nanjo City, it moved here in 2002). You can choose white or red soup, and the pork-bone-based white soup comes with pork spare ribs that have some bite. So popular that the parking lot fills up before opening.
t: I ate here in May 2023 😄
Yutakaya Soba (near Okinawa Prefectural Comprehensive Athletic Park)

It opens at 11, but right before that 4–5 cars all at once were waiting in the parking lot. Since I'd made the effort to arrive first, I hurriedly got out of the car and waited at the entrance to be the first one in ^^;
The shop is a red-tiled old house. A very Okinawan-looking building that tourists will probably love 😄
Menu (apparently the shop was originally in Nanjo City and moved here in 2002 😊)
Menu (it seems you can choose white or red soup)
This time I ordered the "soki soba" with the regular soup (white).
Soki soba (white soup) ¥850
I came with no prior information, but first I took a sip of the soup. A pork-bone-based broth 😄 The noodles are medium-thick, straight-ish with a slight wave. Slightly on the soft side.
Unlike at other shops, the pork spare ribs (soki) are a bit lightly seasoned and tender, but not melt-in-your-mouth — they have some bite.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty, but the soki weren't the deeply flavored, melt-in-your-mouth type; they still had a bit of sinew left.

よね食堂.name: Yone Shokudo
よね食堂.desc: A long-established diner with banners flying that read "Founded 1957". The signature Yone soba has a soup where you can taste both chicken and pork, medium-thin gently wavy noodles, and an everything-on-top lineup of soft-bone pork ribs, bone-in pork ribs, and braised pork belly.
t: I ate here in February 2024 😁
Yone Shokudo
In Yone Shokudo's parking lot there's a banner reading "Founded 1957"! A long-established shop 😄
Menu

There was a "Yone soba", which shares the shop's name, so I ordered it. The toppings are soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) — an everything-on-top kind of bowl 😆
The soba menu is extensive, but the set meal menu is extensive too 😄
Celebrity autographs posted inside the shop

Inside, there were celebrity autographs on the wall, but I couldn't make out whose they were (^0^;) One says "All Japan Pro Wrestling", so it's from some pro wrestler, and below I can also see what is probably Yoko Gushiken's autograph 😆
Yone soba ¥800
The "Yone soba" has arrived. First, a sip of the soup. It's a soup where you can taste both chicken and pork.
Yone soba ¥800
Next I try the noodles. Medium-thin, gently wavy, soft noodles.
The toppings — braised pork belly, bone-in pork ribs, and soft-bone pork ribs — are tender too, but have a sinewy texture.
Rating (9/15): Simply tasty. It's relatively close to Naha Airport, so why not try this long-established flavor at least once 😁
